companions.name: NGC 6362 V40 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary NGC 6362 V40, 0.7947 solar masses and 0.997 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 5.296 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 0.997 +/- 0.013, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 0.7947 +/- 0.0048, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.785 +/- 0.011, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K): 6095 K

orbit.source: NGC 6362 V40: P 5.2961725 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2453915.50966 (Section II.1, after Equation (1)); i 88.22 degrees (Table 4, column V40); e 0.05054, omega 206.6 degrees (Table 4, column V40); stored +180 degrees: as published the companion would pass behind 7.3 h from the published secondary-minimum ephemeris (Eq. 1); +180 puts it within 0.01 h, and it fits the paper's Table 3 radial velocities. HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of NGC 6362 V40, a pair that eclipse each other every 5.296 days.
text.introduction: It has 0.7947 solar masses and 0.997 solar radii; its partner has 0.8337 and 1.3253, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), NGC 6362 V40: Mass, Radius and Period, from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)
